validity.recommendation: Keep the row; it is a real, distinct gas lateral. Fix the capacity units and the start endpoint (see the two concern findings below).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. The row rests on a single citation (Shafaq, 9 backlinks) reprinting a Feb-2021 Iraqi Ministry of Oil press release: 'The Ministry of Oil completes a 22 km pipeline that supplies al-Qayyarah Power Plant' — a 22 km, 18-inch dry-gas line branching off the Baiji-Mosul (power-plant) gas trunk and running to the al-Qayyarah power station in Nineveh, built in <3 months by the Baghdad and North Projects Commissions, with seven crossings at road intersections/valleys. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION that the plant is a gas plant fed by such a line: peer-reviewed IIETA study of 'Al-Qayyarah Gas Power Plant' (six frame-9E units, ~750 MW, running on natural gas). So the physical asset and its gas-supply function are real. CLASSIFICATION: correct — this is a short single-purpose lateral/feeder to one power plant; GEM's PipelineType='distribution' is appropriate (it is NOT a transmission trunk, and NOT an oil/NGL line — none of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines matches a Mosul->Qayyarah gas spur). DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. It taps the Baiji-Mosul gas trunk (roster P1842 'Baiji-Al Mushraq Gas Pipeline', ?->Mosul, 18-in) but is a distinct 22 km spur to the power station — the wiki slug 'Baiji-Mousal-Al_Qayyarah' just records that tie-in. No other roster row is the same physical pipe. ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Oil Pipelines Co' and Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' are both supported by the press release (operated by the Pipeline Company; a Ministry of Oil project; built by the Oil Projects Company / SCOP). Length 22 km, diameter 18 in, and start Feb-2021 all match the source.

validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity/CapacityUnits. 130 bcm/y is impossible; the source's '130' is almost certainly ~130 mmcf/d (~1.34 bcm/y). Re-source the flow figure before re-stating; do not keep 130 bcm/y.
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY IS WRONG. GEM records Capacity=130.00 bcm/y. The sole cited source (Shafaq / Ministry of Oil) states the line is '22 km-130 cubic feet' — a garbled unit, not a real bcm/y figure. 130 bcm/y is physically absurd: it is roughly the ENTIRE annual gas throughput of Iraq's national system and cannot pass through a 22 km / 18-inch spur feeding a single ~750 MW power station. A 750 MW gas plant consumes on the order of ~120-140 million cubic feet per day, so the source '130' most plausibly means ~130 mmcf/d (~1.34 bcm/y) — a ~100x units error in the GEM cell. I did not find an independent source stating the flow in explicit units (the academic paper gives plant MW, not gas volume), so I am NOT proposing a corrected number to auto-apply — flagging it for human correction of the units/magnitude. As-entered value is not defensible.

validity.recommendation: Revise the start endpoint. The line does not begin in Mosul city; it ties into the Baiji-Mosul gas trunk ~22 km from the Qayyarah power station. Set StartLocation to the tie-in on the Baiji-Mosul trunk near Qayyarah (Nineveh), not 'Mousal'.
validity.researcher_notes: START ENDPOINT MISLEADING. GEM StartLocation='Mousal' (Mosul), EndLocation='Al Qayyarah PS', both Nineveh. But Qayyarah lies ~60 km SOUTH of Mosul on the Tigris, while the line is only 22 km long — it cannot run from Mosul city to Qayyarah. The source is explicit that the pipe branches off the existing 'main pipeline (Baiji-Mosul power plant)' gas trunk and runs to the al-Qayyarah power station. So the true origin is a tie-in point on the Baiji-Mosul trunk roughly 22 km from the plant (near Qayyarah), NOT Mosul. Naming the start 'Mousal' overstates the corridor. End ('Al Qayyarah PS', Nineveh) is correct. This is a locate/attribution fix, not an existence problem.

fills.researcher_notes: Operator ref was blank. Ministry of Oil press release states the line is operated by the Pipeline Company (Oil Pipelines Company), consistent with GEM's Operator value. Single official source -> medium.

Owner ref was blank. The project is a Ministry of Oil undertaking (built by the state Oil Projects Company/SCOP, operated by the state Oil Pipelines Company), consistent with GEM Owner='Iraq Ministry of Oil' 100%. Single official source -> medium.

routes.corridor_desc: Short (~22 km) gas lateral entirely within southern Nineveh governorate. It branches off the pre-existing Baiji-Mosul gas trunk pipeline and runs to the al-Qayyarah power station near Qayyarah town on the west bank of the Tigris, ~60 km south of Mosul. Source notes seven crossings at major road intersections plus valleys/terrain. The end (power station near Qayyarah, ~35.80N, 43.28E) is well bounded to the town area; the exact station coordinate and the tie-in point on the trunk are NOT independently sourced, so the start coordinate is left null and only loosely bounded to a point ~22 km (by pipe length) from the plant along the Baiji-Mosul corridor.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the Ministry of Oil release (branch off Baiji-Mosul trunk -> al-Qayyarah power station) and Qayyarah town coordinates from Wikipedia (35.80N, 43.283E, west bank of Tigris ~60 km S of Mosul). The end coordinate is the Qayyarah town/plant area (approximate; exact plant coordinate not independently sourced). Start tie-in coordinate NOT fabricated — left null; it lies ~22 km from the plant along the Baiji-Mosul gas corridor. No coordinates were invented.

summary: Real 22 km/18-in gas lateral to al-Qayyarah power station (existence + classification confirmed, not a duplicate); staged 2 concerns — Capacity 130 bcm/y is impossible (~100x units error, source says garbled '130 cubic feet', likely ~130 mmcf/d) and start endpoint 'Mousal' is wrong (line taps the Baiji-Mosul trunk ~22 km from the plant, not Mosul city).
